name: Brainstem
summary: The brain's oldest structure, connecting the cerebrum to the spinal cord. Controls breathing, heartbeat, sleep-wake cycles, and consciousness.

connections.note: Master alertness switch projecting to cortex via thalamus.

facts.text: Ten of the twelve cranial nerves originate from the brainstem — controlling facial expressions, eye movements, taste, hearing, and swallowing.
The reticular activating system (RAS) running through the brainstem is the master alertness switch. Damage to it can cause coma.

detailedDescription: The brainstem connects the cerebrum to the spinal cord. The Midbrain contains the superior and inferior colliculi and controls eye movement. The Pons bridges cerebrum-cerebellum communication and regulates breathing. The Medulla Oblongata controls heartbeat, blood pressure, breathing rhythm, and protective reflexes. All ascending and descending pathways pass through the brainstem.
